title: SAFETY LAYERS IN ALIGNED LARGE LANGUAGE MODELS: THE KEY TO LLM SECURITY
motivation: Aligned LLMs suffer security degradation during fine-tuning attacks, even with harmless datasets, posing real-world deployment risks
problem_framing: Understanding the parameter-level mechanism by which aligned LLMs distinguish malicious from normal queries, and how to preserve security during fine-tuning
key_insight: A small contiguous set of middle layers (safety layers) are responsible for security recognition; freezing these layers during fine-tuning preserves model security
method_signature: SPPFT: freeze safety layer gradients during fine-tuning, update only non-safety layer parameters
evaluation_criteria: Harmful rate and harmful score on malicious query dataset; AlpacaEval 2.0 for performance; over-rejection count for localization
negative_result_or_admitted_limitation: Wei et al.'s discrete neuron freezing strategy did not suffice in preventing security degradation; freezing non-safety layers does not preserve security and may even exacerbate issues
evidence_for_taste: the precise nature and implications of security alignments in LLMs still remain unclear
underscoring the generalizability of our findings across different aligned LLMs

thinking_moves: Analyze layer-wise vector differences between normal and malicious query processing to discover where divergence occurs
